_comment: Hand-authored. The weapon handler jump tables and the weapon-by-level stat tables in bank 6, and the spawn-command table in bank 7.

regions.name: Weapon object handlers A: 12 entries
regions.description: Inline jump table after JSR $85F4 at $8650, indexed by $3C, the selected weapon; entries are targets minus one. Registered in annotations/dispatch.json, where the count's argument is: 24 bytes between the JSR and traced code at $866B.

regions.name: Weapon object handlers B: 13 entries
regions.description: Inline jump table after JSR $85F4 at $86E4, indexed by $3C (0-12, the status cursor's range); entries are targets minus one. Registered in annotations/dispatch.json.

regions.name: Spawn-script commands: 3 entries
regions.description: Inline jump table after JSR $D6AE at $F7C6 in the spawn-script interpreter: 0 wait, 1 jump, 2 end. CMP #$03 / BCS before it bounds the index. Registered in annotations/dispatch.json.

regions.name: Weapon attack by level (to $05A8)
regions.description: $86AF computes Y = $3D x 11 + $3C - the selected weapon's level times eleven plus the weapon - and $86C1-$86DC read four tables with it: LDA $86F5,Y, $8716,Y, $8737,Y and $8758,Y. A weapon object exists only at level 1-3 and for weapons 1-11, so Y runs 12-44 and each table's bytes are its base + 12 to base + 44: 33 entries, 11 weapons x 3 levels. The read BASES are 12 bytes before the tables - the overlap trick again; at $86F5 those 12 bytes are the tail of the weapon jump table. CORRECTION: tools/find-tables.py claimed the four as 33-byte tables at the read bases, which put the first on top of the jump table. This one ($86F5 base): a non-zero entry replaces the object's $05A8, its attack.
